fields.description:
Test PPP forecasts using only information available before each prediction, then compare them with later results that were not used to build the model.

This follows [SCRUM-476](https://basketball-strategy.atlassian.net/browse/SCRUM-476). The current calibration report uses a fixed Ridge model, trains on earlier seasons, and evaluates a later season. However, it also uses statistics from the season being evaluated, so it does not prove pre-game forecasting accuracy. This task adds a separate forecasting evaluation.

To complete this task:

* Define when the prediction is made and how far ahead it predicts. Record when every input would have been available.
* Build the inputs from earlier information only. Do not use future games, future seasons, or the results being predicted.
* Reserve later data for the final test. Use only earlier data to choose features and model settings and to fit scaling or other data preparation steps.
* Compare the forecast model with a baseline that follows the same timing rules, using the same untouched test rows. Report prediction errors, calibration, sample counts, and limitations.
* Add tests showing that changing future data cannot change earlier prediction inputs or data preparation fitted on earlier training data.
* Document the test procedure and code and dataset versions so someone else can reproduce the results.

fields.description:
Measure the deployed analyst Top-K uplift endpoint with a small bounded run, review the observations and propose targets for team review.

Acceptance criteria:

* Record the deployment, /metrics/topk-uplift request inputs, sample sizes and response times.

* Keep the current hosting limits and budget.

comments.body:
Actions:

* Ran quick checks comparing predicted PPP vs baseline PPP across sample plays.
* Looked at high-level distributions to verify predictions are in a reasonable range (no extreme unrealistic PPP values).

Result:

* No obvious calibration disasters detected, but we have not fully tuned calibration yet.

Assessment:

* Probability medium.
* Impact high; we explicitly call this out as a limitation when discussing ML vs baseline in the defence.

I added checks for whether predicted points per possession (PPP) are too high or too low, plus a comparison chart in SCRUM-476 ([b9f145d](https://github.com/Basketball-Capstone-25/NBAPlayRanker/commit/b9f145d15189dd7f6be6854166bce0aef3f58f01)). The calculation tests passed as part of the 176 backend tests, but I still need to check the analyst page in the browser. The model trains on earlier seasons and tests on later ones, but it still uses statistics from the season being tested, so this does not prove it can predict future games. The risk status is unchanged for now; [SCRUM-526](https://basketball-strategy.atlassian.net/browse/SCRUM-526) will test predictions using only information available beforehand.

I compared the calibration API results with the analyst page in SCRUM-476 and checked the calculations in BST-123/124. The report covers 1,650 test rows from five seasons, and its design is saved in Visual Paradigm revision 51.

I moved the risk back to Monitoring because the report still uses same-season statistics and does not prove how well this model or the other recommendation models will predict future games. I will keep checking whether predictions are too high or too low and whether each group has enough results; SCRUM-526 covers testing with information available before the prediction.

The calibration calculation passed its recorded checks, but it uses rates from the season being evaluated. The remaining work is to test predictions with information available before the prediction time.

The season-ahead model overpredicted by 0.02227 PPP on average, compared with 0.01845 for the prior-league baseline. Lower RMSE did not remove this bias. Keep Monitoring and check a separate later season before claiming good calibration. [Results](https://github.com/Basketball-Capstone-25/NBAPlayRanker/blob/ba814406a69c6de23f14af06a28f153eaa436fdc/docs/iteration-15/forecast/README.md).

Mitigation Strategy.value: Track PPP bias and error by season and play type. Evaluate lagged predictors on untouched chronological holdouts before making forecasting claims; report small groups and unsupported results.

comments.body:
Actions:

* Used a season-wise time split for evaluation to reduce leakage from future to past.
* Compared training vs validation performance to look for large gaps.

Result:

* Early checks show some risk of overfitting but not catastrophic; we are not claiming production-grade generalization.

Assessment:

* Probability medium.
* Impact high; this remains an important limitation of the prototype model.

The earlier note acknowledged overfitting as a limitation, so Resolved is too strong. A season split alone does not establish generalization when the predictors include information from the evaluated season.

SCRUM-526 fixed eight features, chose Ridge alpha on an earlier tuning season and kept the final season outside selection. The 330 team/play-type rows are related observations from one season, so this does not establish generalization. Keep Monitoring until a separate later season is evaluated. [Split and limits](https://github.com/Basketball-Capstone-25/NBAPlayRanker/blob/ba814406a69c6de23f14af06a28f153eaa436fdc/docs/iteration-15/forecast/README.md).

Mitigation Strategy.value: Compare training and untouched time-holdout error with strictly available predictors. Record model settings, sample size and baseline performance before changing model complexity.

fields.description: Not using strict time splits leaks future info into training, inflating metrics.
fields.summary: Data leakage inflates results

comments.body:
Actions:

* Reviewed feature engineering to avoid including direct outcome-like fields in the inputs.
* Used time-based splits to make sure future information does not leak into training.

Result:

* No obvious direct leakage features remain in the current feature set.

Assessment:

* Probability reduced to medium.
* Impact high if leakage is discovered later, so we continue to treat evaluation results as approximate.

I changed the calibration code so it calculates scaling and reliability values from the training seasons only ([b9f145d](https://github.com/Basketball-Capstone-25/NBAPlayRanker/commit/b9f145d15189dd7f6be6854166bce0aef3f58f01)). BST-123 passed the checks for keeping later-season results out of those calculations. The model still uses some statistics from the season being tested, which may not be available before a game. I am keeping this risk under Monitoring, with [SCRUM-526](https://basketball-strategy.atlassian.net/browse/SCRUM-526) covering tests that use only earlier information.

BST-123 passed the checks that keep training seasons separate from test seasons and prepare the data using training rows only. I checked that the analyst page explains these splits and limitations, with the design saved in Visual Paradigm revision 51.

The inputs still include statistics from the season being tested, so the earlier broad claims about preventing all data leakage are not proof of future-game accuracy. This risk stays under Monitoring, and SCRUM-526 remains To Do to check which inputs are available before a prediction.

Training and test seasons are separated, but the current diagnostic still uses same-season rate features. Keep the timing of every predictor in the next evaluation so future information cannot enter a forecasting claim.

The shot model uses the location and type of the shot actually taken, while BST-117 expects information available before the possession. Those inputs can describe conditional shot quality, but they do not establish a pre-possession forecast. Document the prediction moment and feature availability before the repaired dataset is used for holdout or cross-validation claims.

Changing the final season's points, possessions and rates left the selected model, fitted scaling and predictions unchanged in the new forecast tests. Inputs now come from the prior regular season. Monitoring remains because the CSV has no publication timestamps and the shot-model timing issue is separate. [Timing checks](https://github.com/Basketball-Capstone-25/NBAPlayRanker/blob/ba814406a69c6de23f14af06a28f153eaa436fdc/docs/iteration-15/forecast/README.md).

Mitigation Strategy.value: Define the prediction moment and whether each feature is observed, lagged or supplied as a planned action. Fit preprocessing on training data only and use an untouched time holdout. Do not present conditional or retrospective estimates as prospective accuracy.

comments.body:
Actions:

* Implemented PPP_pred and ran evaluation against PPP_baseline using RMSE.
* Prepared to present ML vs baseline accuracy honestly in the defence, including any limitations.

Result:

* Model accuracy is acceptable for a prototype but not guaranteed production-level; we treat the ML model as an enhancement over a solid baseline.

Assessment:

* Probability medium.
* Impact high; clearly communicated as a technical risk and limitation rather than hidden.

Elaboration review: probability High; impact Serious. Reviewed the assessment and updated the mitigation plan.  
Next action: Run and record one reproducible baseline-versus-ML comparison.  
Current mitigation result: not established by this planning update; record the actual observation after the check.  
Next review: within seven days, or sooner if the trigger occurs.
The existing evaluation reports retrospective PPP error and uplift. A meaningful baseline comparison with strictly lagged inputs is still To Do, so model improvement remains an open risk.

The timed baseline comparison is complete: Ridge RMSE was 0.06712 versus 0.06817 for the prior-league baseline on the same 330 rows. That small one-season improvement, with higher bias, is not enough to claim a reliable benefit. Keep Monitoring; the next check needs a separately collected later season. [Comparison](https://github.com/Basketball-Capstone-25/NBAPlayRanker/blob/ba814406a69c6de23f14af06a28f153eaa436fdc/docs/iteration-15/forecast/README.md).

Mitigation Strategy.value: Compare model and baseline on the same prediction task and held-out period. Diagnose feature and data problems before tuning, and report a lack of improvement when that is the result.

fields.summary: Changed API contracts may break existing pages

comments.body: I added the Top-K comparison API and documented its JSON and CSV results in [5092bf1](https://github.com/Basketball-Capstone-25/NBAPlayRanker/commit/5092bf1d93ed7c30f2e2b7b34eddd613f4ece474). The tests in `backend/tests/test_topk_uplift.py` passed checks for matching export values, correct headers, invalid inputs, empty results and user permissions (BST-122). The local checks passed: 176 backend tests, 12 frontend tests, TypeScript and the production build. I still need to check the deployed API and real accounts in BST-127/128 before calling the live version verified.

I moved this risk to Active because the API tests passed but the browser downloads still failed. SCRUM-527 fixed the missing sign-in information, but the download entries then showed Stopped, so BST-129 remains Fail. I added a new download route in c3044da that serves files through the website, and all 33 frontend tests, TypeScript and the build passed. I still need to deploy it and confirm that a downloaded file actually saves and opens.

I moved this risk back to Monitoring after deploying c3044da and confirming that the Data Explorer CSV finishes downloading and opens. The 12 signed-in download and permission checks passed, along with all 33 frontend tests and GitHub CI. The other file types passed HTTP response checks at this stage; the actual browser save was confirmed for the Data Explorer CSV. I kept the earlier failures in BST-129 and will repeat the download and permission checks after future deployments.

I found that the coach Matchup PDF route, `/export/playtype-viz.pdf`, was missing from the new download route's allowed list. I moved this risk back to Active and reopened BST-129 as Fail while I add and deploy that route under SCRUM-527. The earlier analyst CSV, shot CSV and shot-plan PDF results still stand. I need to test the coach PDF after deployment before returning this risk to Monitoring.

I added the missing coach Matchup PDF route in [18baffc](https://github.com/Basketball-Capstone-25/NBAPlayRanker/commit/18baffc0cc6f99273f60e797a499804029b8b84f) and deployed it to https://nbaplayranker-seven.vercel.app. The coach ranking CSV and play-type PDF, analyst Data Explorer and Shot Explorer CSVs, and shot-plan PDF all saved with readable content.

The 34 frontend tests, TypeScript, build, [GitHub checks](https://github.com/Basketball-Capstone-25/NBAPlayRanker/actions/runs/37157802665) and 14 signed-in download checks passed. BST-129 is now Pass and the risk is back to Monitoring, with these downloads to be checked again after future releases.
The export fixes passed, but the wider audit found shot-page role mismatches and an incompatible analysis response. Those separate contracts remain broken and should keep this risk active.

Mitigation Strategy.value: Link each failing page/API contract to a bug and test. Verify parameter names, response fields and roles together before closing the failure.

I deployed backend commit e950869 as Cloud Run revision nba-playranker-api-00005-hrn and checked it after startup. Coach recommendations and analyst data/calibration requests worked, confirming that the new deployment could load the required data and model files. I recorded the deployment and rollback details and kept the existing resource and sign-in settings. This risk is now Monitoring, and I will repeat the data-loading and recommendation checks after future deployments.

The recorded backend deployment loaded the data and model files needed for its smoke checks. Later releases still need a versioned artifact set and a recovery check, especially while the shot-data repair is pending.

The isolated missing-data check stopped startup with a traceback naming the Synergy file. A separate process without Supabase configuration still returned a healthy liveness response. Define the production startup and readiness checks and provide clear recovery errors; the deployed service passed its health checks.

Mitigation Strategy.value: Version runtime data, model files and configuration together. Validate production prerequisites with clear diagnostics, distinguish liveness from readiness and verify recovery from a clean checkout before replacing the release.

fields.summary: Free-plan limits or inactivity may pause Supabase

I found that Basketball Playtype Ranker was paused in Supabase and could not resume because an owner had reached the limit of two active free projects.

I recorded this as Active, with Very High probability and Serious impact.

The dashboard said the data and backups were safe and the project could resume until June 1, 2027.

The live database tests in `supabase/tests/gameplan_state_verification.sql` passed the ownership, permission and data-validation checks in BST-125/126, and I removed the temporary test data by rolling back the test transactions. I still need to test coach and analyst sign-in through the browser in BST-128. I will check availability again before the next demo because a free project can pause again.

Supabase is running on the Free plan again, and the earlier problem resuming the project is cleared. I tested real coach and analyst sign-in, profile permissions and Gameplan database access; all 49 live API/database checks passed and the relevant browser pages worked.

I removed the temporary test data and moved this risk from Active to Monitoring. I will check availability before demos and after periods of inactivity.

The recorded sign-in and database checks passed after the project resumed on Free. That resolves the earlier pause, but availability after inactivity and free-project capacity still need checking before a demo.

Mitigation Strategy.value: Check project status and sign-in before the demo, preserve backups and identify the service owner. Do not upgrade a plan or pause another owner's project without the required agreement.

fields.description:
Use cases: UC69.

Scope: The listed local component/API checks; production observations are identified separately.

Preconditions: install the pinned development dependencies and use the repository fixtures.

Run:  
python -m pytest backend/tests/test_access_control.py -q

Check these inputs and results:

1. With the development-auth switch enabled and validate_session(None). Expected: Session validation returns True.
2. With development bypass disabled and validate_session(None). Expected: Session validation returns False.
3. With development bypass disabled and the JWT verifier returning no claims. Expected: Session validation returns False.
4. With development bypass disabled and verified claims with a subject and valid expiry. Expected: Session validation returns True.

Related cases: BST-45, BST-46, BST-47, BST-48.

Evidence: docs/assignment-1-revision/tests/backend-junit.xml and frontend-vitest.json.  
Browser steps: load Matchup as coach; sign out; open /matchup; sign in as analyst with next=/matchup. Expect rankings for the coach, a login redirect after sign-out and Data Explorer for the analyst. Evidence: matchup-browser.txt, session-signout-browser.txt and analyst-role-redirect.txt.
fields.summary: Session validation accepts verified tokens and rejects missing or invalid tokens

comments.body: Session validation returned the expected result for all four local configurations. Signing out also returned the browser to the public page and blocked the coach route.

fields.description:
Use cases: UC65.

Scope: The listed local component/API checks; production observations are identified separately.

Preconditions: install the pinned development dependencies and use the repository fixtures.

Run:  
python -m pytest backend/tests/test_ridge_model.py -q

Check these inputs and results:

1. With the configured Ridge pipeline. Expected: The two steps are StandardScaler followed by Ridge with RIDGE_ALPHA.
2. With 200 seeded synthetic rows with the declared feature count. Expected: All 200 predictions are finite and have the expected one-dimensional shape.
3. With 200 seeded synthetic rows. Expected: Every coefficient is finite and their L2 norm is below 50.
4. With five-fold evaluation of the retained historical play-type dataset. Expected: Ridge mean RMSE is below the league-mean baseline RMSE.
5. With the earlier 80% of seasons for training and the remaining seasons for prediction. Expected: All predicted PPP values are between 0 and 2.5.
6. With five-fold evaluation of the retained historical dataset. Expected: Ridge RMSE is below 0.50 in each fold.
7. With the retained offense dataset and declared feature columns. Expected: X is two-dimensional with the declared feature count; y is one-dimensional; row counts match and all values are finite.
8. With the same 300 seeded synthetic rows with alpha 0.001, RIDGE_ALPHA and 10.0. Expected: Coefficient norms decrease strictly from the low alpha through the configured alpha to the high alpha.

Related cases: BST-88, BST-89, BST-90, BST-91, BST-92, BST-93, BST-94, BST-95.

Evidence: docs/assignment-1-revision/tests/backend-junit.xml and frontend-vitest.json.  
This is a historical diagnostic using contemporaneous features. It does not establish future-game forecast accuracy; SCRUM-526 covers that work.
fields.summary: Ridge model meets the documented historical evaluation checks

comments.body: The Ridge checks passed for pipeline structure, finite predictions, regularization and historical error thresholds. Prospective evaluation remains separate work in SCRUM-526.

fields.description:
Use-case coverage: UC62.

This is a startup/readiness contract gap. Missing auth configuration still fails closed at protected endpoints; the result does not demonstrate a security bypass.

Steps:

1. In an isolated child process, suppress dotenv file loading.
2. Make Path.exists return false only for synergy_playtypes_2019_2025_players.csv.
3. Import the backend startup module and capture exit status and error output.

Expected result: A clear controlled error is returned or logged without an unhandled exception.

Current result: Fail. Startup exited 1 with an unhandled FileNotFoundError while importing the context recommender. The traceback identified the dataset path, but there was no controlled startup diagnostic.

Scope: Only the child process saw the simulated missing file; the real dataset and production service were unchanged.

Evidence: docs/assignment-1-revision/tests/additional-local-checks.json.
fields.summary: Missing play-type dataset has a controlled error

Before testing: Use a small dataset with multiple teams, seasons and play types, unequal possession counts, and a documented calculation.

Steps:

1. Calculate the team-season average PPP and selected Top-K PPP by hand, using the documented possession weighting.
2. Compare the calculation and API results with those values, including the PPP difference and any percentage difference.
3. Change another team or season and check that it does not affect the selected team-season average.
4. Test zero or invalid denominators and too little usable data.

Expected: The values match the independent calculation within the stated tolerance, and the reference includes only the intended team and season. Invalid denominators produce a documented safe result or error. The result is clearly described as a historical modeled comparison, without claiming held-out accuracy or a proven improvement caused by the recommendations.
fields.summary: Top-K uplift matches possession-weighted calculations

comments.body:
I checked the uplift calculation with a worked example: a team average of 1.75 points per possession and 2.05 for the selected plays should give a +0.30 difference. The tests in [5092bf1](https://github.com/Basketball-Capstone-25/NBAPlayRanker/commit/5092bf1d93ed7c30f2e2b7b34eddd613f4ece474) returned that result and still used the full team-season average when only one play was selected.

The tests also kept teams and seasons separate and handled negative differences, zero averages and unusable data correctly. BST-127/128 still need live testing; this historical comparison does not prove the plays will improve future results.

The uplift calculation passed on the live backend from [e950869](https://github.com/Basketball-Capstone-25/NBAPlayRanker/commit/e950869cb318c6b44220d3c06be4ba2aa16521da).

The independent example matched +0.30 PPP, with team/season separation and invalid-data checks passing.

For TOR vs BOS in 2024-25 with three plays, JSON and CSV both showed 0.969238 team-average PPP, 1.071696 modeled PPP and a 0.102458 difference.

Results are in live-verification.json; these are historical comparisons, not proof of actual or future improvement.

The Top-K tests passed again, including independently calculated possession-weighted PPP, the team-season reference, negative uplift, zero denominators and invalid input. Changes to other teams and seasons do not enter the selected reference.

Evidence: [backend-junit.xml](https://github.com/Basketball-Capstone-25/NBAPlayRanker/blob/main/docs/assignment-1-revision/tests/backend-junit.xml), [backend.log](https://github.com/Basketball-Capstone-25/NBAPlayRanker/blob/main/docs/assignment-1-revision/tests/backend.log).

Steps:

2. Check the CSV file type and name, and the JSON fields and structure.

Before testing: Use several seasons of identifiable test rows, with later-season values that differ from the training data.

Steps:

1. Inspect the reported training/test splits and record the rows used to fit the model.
2. Check that every training season is earlier than the test season and no held-out row is used for training.
3. Check that raw PPP is excluded from FEATURE_COLS and that the report explains that some other inputs are same-season rates tied to the outcome.
4. Change the held-out target values and feature scale, then check that the training-only inputs and fitted preprocessing settings stay unchanged.

Expected: Training and test rows stay separate and in time order. Scaling and reliability adjustments use only training data, and raw PPP is not an input. Changing the test data does not change fitted training settings, while the evaluation results respond as expected. The report explains that same-season inputs make this a historical evaluation; it does not prove future-game accuracy or rule out every outcome-related input. Using only earlier information and an untouched forecasting test set remains SCRUM-526.
fields.summary: Calibration trains on earlier seasons only

The live report matched 1,650 held-out rows across five seasons in live-verification.json.

The model excludes held-out PPP from training but still uses same-season shooting/scoring rates, so pre-game accuracy remains separate work in SCRUM-526.

I clarified the test description to say exactly what passed: earlier-season training, separate later-season test rows, training-only scaling and reliability calculations, and no raw PPP target used as an input.

I also checked that the report explains its limitation: some other inputs come from the season being evaluated, so this does not prove future-game prediction accuracy.

SCRUM-526 still covers using earlier information and a separate forecasting test set.

Training used earlier seasons, and changing the test-season outcomes did not change the training process or predictions. The live report kept that season order. These are historical results using same-season rates, so they do not prove future-game accuracy.

fields.description:
Use cases: UC16 Export KPIs / Reports; UC49 Export Results (CSV/PDF).    
Feature: SCRUM-486.

Steps: Download CSV, JSON and PDF from each page. Inspect the filename, content type and actual file contents. Use a fixture with commas, quotes, line breaks and special characters in text values.

Expected: Each filename identifies the report and format. The content type matches a valid readable file. Text characters do not break CSV columns, JSON parsing or PDF rendering.

Execution results are recorded in the comments.
fields.summary: Downloaded reports have readable filenames and content

comments.body: Fail. A Context download for margin -2 used _2_ in the filename, so it could not be distinguished from a +2 report by name. The JSON contents kept margin -2 correctly. The filename formatter needs to preserve the minus sign. Fix: SCRUM-616.

Pass on retest. The filename fix now keeps margin -2 in all three Context downloads. CSV and JSON values match, and the PDFs open with the expected rows. The formatter tests cover quotes, commas, line breaks and special characters. The earlier failure remains above and links to SCRUM-616.
